# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

  --text-secondary: #52514e;

  /* ...only the roles this chart uses */

@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root:where(:not([data-theme="light"])) .viz-root {
    color-scheme: dark;
    --surface-1:      #1a1a19;
    --text-primary:   #f0efec;
    --text-secondary: #c3c2b7;
    --series-1:       #3987e5;

  --surface-1:      #1a1a19;

import glob, os, re, json
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from lmfit.models import LorentzianModel, LinearModel

files = glob.glob(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "spectrum_*.csv"))
files = sorted(files, key=lambda f: float(re.search(r"spectrum_([\d.]+)nm", f).group(1)))
WIN = {"LA": (158, 196), "Eprime": (340, 372), "A1g": (400, 440), "Si": (508, 534)}
res = []
for f in files:
    lam = float(re.search(r"spectrum_([\d.]+)nm", f).group(1))
    EL = 1239.84/lam
    df = pd.read_csv(f); x = df["shift_cm1"].values; y = df["intensity"].values
    row = {"lam_nm": lam, "E_L_eV": round(EL, 4)}
    for name, (a, b) in WIN.items():
        m = (x >= a) & (x <= b)
        xx, yy = x[m], y[m]
        lor = LorentzianModel(prefix="p_")
        lin = LinearModel(prefix="b_")
        pars = lin.make_params(intercept=np.median(yy[:5]+yy[-5:])/2, slope=0)
        c0 = xx[np.argmax(yy)]
        pars += lor.make_params(center=dict(value=c0, min=a, max=b), amplitude=dict(value=max(yy.max()-yy.min(), 1)*np.pi*2, min=0), sigma=dict(value=3, min=0.5, max=20))
        mod = lor + lin
        out = mod.fit(yy, pars, x=xx)
        p = out.params
        row[f"{name}_pos"] = round(p["p_center"].value, 2)
        row[f"{name}_pos_se"] = round(p["p_center"].stderr or np.nan, 2)
        row[f"{name}_FWHM"] = round(2*p["p_sigma"].value, 2)
        row[f"{name}_area"] = round(p["p_amplitude"].value, 0)
        row[f"{name}_snr"] = round(p["p_amplitude"].value/np.pi/p["p_sigma"].value / max(np.std(yy - out.best_fit), 1), 1)
    res.append(row)
df = pd.DataFrame(res)
pd.set_option("display.width", 250); pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
print(df[["lam_nm","E_L_eV","LA_pos","LA_pos_se","LA_FWHM","LA_area","Eprime_pos","Eprime_pos_se","Eprime_FWHM","Eprime_area","A1g_pos","A1g_pos_se","A1g_FWHM","A1g_area","Si_pos","Si_FWHM","Si_area"]].to_string(index=False))
df.to_csv(os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "raman_analysis", "fits.csv"), index=False)

input.summary: The WS2 flake is strongly resonant between about 585 and 601 nm (2.06–2.12 eV). The A1g band's integrated area is flat at about 0.8–0.9×10⁶ counts across 585–601 nm, drops to about 0.4 at 605 nm and 0.09 at 618 nm, and is about 100× weaker at 627 nm and about 700× weaker at 638 nm. The off-resonant spectra are close to noise, so the 626.9 and 638.4 nm numbers are effectively upper limits. A broad background rises sharply on the same resonance, and re-plotted on absolute emission energy it converges near 2.00–2.02 eV, which points to photoluminescence (PL) from excitons or trions rather than Raman scattering. The E′–A1g separation is 60.75 ± 0.24 cm⁻¹ (585–611 nm), which is consistent with a monolayer or few-layer flake but does not fix the layer number. No consistent strain or doping signal is resolved in the peak positions. The strongest cautions are: the excitation-dependent intensity mixes the electronic resonance with laser power, optical interference and the PL background, and the low-shift and high-shift ends of the spectra are shaped by filter edges.

observations.finding: A1g (~418 cm⁻¹) is the dominant Raman band and is strongly resonant with the 2.06–2.12 eV region. Its integrated area is roughly flat from 585 to 601 nm, then falls steeply.
The E′ (~357 cm⁻¹) and A1g positions are stable within about ±1 cm⁻¹, and their separation is nearly constant across the sweep.
The A1g mode softens by about 0.5 cm⁻¹ on resonance. The 599–611 nm average is 418.07 cm⁻¹, while the 618–638 nm average is 418.59 cm⁻¹, so the resonant spectra sit about 0.5 cm⁻¹ lower.
observations.evidence: Fitted A1g centres; off-resonant mean 418.59 cm⁻¹ (618–638 nm), resonant mean 418.07 cm⁻¹ (599–611 nm). Si 520.7 cm⁻¹ reference fits to 521.6 ± 0.5 cm⁻¹, implying an absolute axis offset of about +0.5–1 cm⁻¹. The 0.5 cm⁻¹ resonant shift is comparable to that offset and to the fit-to-fit scatter, so it is not a significant strain or doping signal on its own.

observations.finding: The broad background is not a fixed Raman shift. When spectra are re-plotted against absolute emission energy (E_L − ħω), the broad humps from the strongly resonant spectra roughly line up near 2.00–2.02 eV, while sharp lines move as expected for Raman scattering. This points to PL from the flake as the origin of the background.
observations.evidence: Re-plot over 1.90–2.20 eV emission energy, shown in ~/raman_analysis/emission.png. Background median counts: 82,811 at 601.4 nm vs 168 at 638.4 nm (about 500×). observations.finding: The LA-like line near 175 cm⁻¹ is weak. Its area is about 6–10% of A1g at 595–601 nm and is not resolvable above background at 579, 618–638 nm.
observations.evidence: LA position 174.1–176.8 cm⁻¹ at 591–611 nm (single Lorentzian, linear baseline); LA/A1g area ratio ≈ 0.06 at 595.5 nm, 0.087 at 599.1 nm, 0.10 at 601.4 nm.

observations.finding: Two extra bands appear that are not fitted and not assigned here: a broad feature near 478–484 cm⁻¹ with height about 0.5× A1g at 591–601 nm, and features near 295 and 330–352 cm⁻¹. toolu_01V8Bzaj422ACP9FtVB5cwG9.summary: The WS2 flake is strongly resonant between about 585 and 601 nm (2.06–2.12 eV). The A1g band's integrated area is flat at about 0.8–0.9×10⁶ counts across 585–601 nm, drops to about 0.4 at 605 nm and 0.09 at 618 nm, and is about 100× weaker at 627 nm and about 700× weaker at 638 nm. The off-resonant spectra are close to noise, so the 626.9 and 638.4 nm numbers are effectively upper limits. A broad background rises sharply on the same resonance, and re-plotted on absolute emission energy it converges near 2.00–2.02 eV, which points to photoluminescence (PL) from excitons or trions rather than Raman scattering. The E′–A1g separation is 60.75 ± 0.24 cm⁻¹ (585–611 nm), which is consistent with a monolayer or few-layer flake but does not fix the layer number. No consistent strain or doping signal is resolved in the peak positions. The strongest cautions are: the excitation-dependent intensity mixes the electronic resonance with laser power, optical interference and the PL background, and the low-shift and high-shift ends of the spectra are shaped by filter edges.

observations.finding: A1g (~418 cm⁻¹) is the dominant Raman band and is strongly resonant with the 2.06–2.12 eV region. Its integrated area is roughly flat from 585 to 601 nm, then falls steeply.
The E′ (~357 cm⁻¹) and A1g positions are stable within about ±1 cm⁻¹, and their separation is nearly constant across the sweep.
The A1g mode softens by about 0.5 cm⁻¹ on resonance. The 599–611 nm average is 418.07 cm⁻¹, while the 618–638 nm average is 418.59 cm⁻¹, so the resonant spectra sit about 0.5 cm⁻¹ lower.
observations.evidence: Fitted A1g centres; off-resonant mean 418.59 cm⁻¹ (618–638 nm), resonant mean 418.07 cm⁻¹ (599–611 nm). Si 520.7 cm⁻¹ reference fits to 521.6 ± 0.5 cm⁻¹, implying an absolute axis offset of about +0.5–1 cm⁻¹. The 0.5 cm⁻¹ resonant shift is comparable to that offset and to the fit-to-fit scatter, so it is not a significant strain or doping signal on its own.

observations.finding: The broad background is not a fixed Raman shift. When spectra are re-plotted against absolute emission energy (E_L − ħω), the broad humps from the strongly resonant spectra roughly line up near 2.00–2.02 eV, while sharp lines move as expected for Raman scattering. This points to PL from the flake as the origin of the background.
observations.evidence: Re-plot over 1.90–2.20 eV emission energy, shown in ~/raman_analysis/emission.png. Background median counts: 82,811 at 601.4 nm vs 168 at 638.4 nm (about 500×). Background values go negative in several spectra (e.g. −117 at 599.1 nm), so the baseline subtraction is imperfect.

observations.finding: The LA-like line near 175 cm⁻¹ is weak. Its area is about 6–10% of A1g at 595–601 nm and is not resolvable above background at 579, 618–638 nm.
observations.evidence: LA position 174.1–176.8 cm⁻¹ at 591–611 nm (single Lorentzian, linear baseline); LA/A1g area ratio ≈ 0.06 at 595.5 nm, 0.087 at 599.1 nm, 0.10 at 601.4 nm.

observations.finding: Two extra bands appear that are not fitted and not assigned here: a broad feature near 478–484 cm⁻¹ with height about 0.5× A1g at 591–601 nm, and features near 295 and 330–352 cm⁻¹. The 350 cm⁻¹ component overlaps E′ and is ambiguous, and its decomposition from E′ is not stable between spectra.
observations.evidence: Peak finder heights at 591.66 nm: 484 cm⁻¹ at 65,040 vs A1g 119,161; at 595.47 nm: 480 cm⁻¹ at 62,866 vs A1g 142,254. The two-component E′ fit at 585 nm gives a ~350 component comparable to E′ in area, but the split swaps between adjacent spectra.

observations.finding: A1g (~418 cm⁻¹) is the dominant Raman band and is strongly resonant with the 2.06–2.12 eV region. Its integrated area is roughly flat from 585 to 601 nm, then falls steeply.
The E′ (~357 cm⁻¹) and A1g positions are stable within about ±1 cm⁻¹, and their separation is nearly constant across the sweep.
The A1g mode softens by about 0.5 cm⁻¹ on resonance. The 599–611 nm average is 418.07 cm⁻¹, while the 618–638 nm average is 418.59 cm⁻¹, so the resonant spectra sit about 0.5 cm⁻¹ lower.

This points to PL from the flake as the origin of the background.

caveats: Intensities are corrected only for spectrometer efficiency. The 0.7 mW nominal power at the sample is not known to be constant across the dye-laser range. Dye-laser output usually changes strongly across a dye's gain curve, so the 579 nm point and the off-resonant tail may be power-limited.

Interference from the 290 nm SiO2 layer modulates both excitation and collection of the Raman signal as a function of wavelength. I did not compute this modulation; it could change intensities by tens of percent over 580–640 nm. It is small compared with the ~700× resonance enhancement but affects the detail of the off-resonant tail and the shape of the resonance profile.

The broad continuum is most likely PL, but it could partly be a resonant background from the flake or substrate. The baseline subtraction is imperfect (negative counts appear in several spectra), so A1g areas carry an estimated ±10–20% systematic error, larger at 599–601 nm where the background is largest.

The low-shift edge at about 140–150 cm⁻¹ is step-like and appears in every spectrum at a roughly fixed shift, which suggests a notch or edge filter transmission edge rather than a Raman band. The roll-off at 650–700 cm⁻¹ coincides with the window edge of the shorter spectra (e.g. 638 nm ends at 673.5 cm⁻¹). Treat the peaks at 640–720 cm⁻¹ in my peak list as artifacts unless a filter-free measurement confirms them.
The 638 nm spectrum contains single-point spikes at about 549 cm⁻¹ and 521 cm⁻¹, likely cosmic rays or a laser plasma line, so they should be excluded from any quantitative use.
Absolute frequencies carry a calibration offset of about +0.5–1 cm⁻¹, judged from the Si 520.7 cm⁻¹ line. Differences such as the E′–A1g separation are much less affected.

The 290 nm SiO2 and the flake's resonance both change with excitation wavelength, so intensity ratios between A1g and the Si line are not reliable here: the Si fits are unstable where the PL background is large (595–605 nm).

The sequential colour ramp used for the stacked plot fails the validator's ordinal ΔL check, which is designed for discrete ordered marks; the spectra are a continuous variable, so I used the monotone sequential ramp. This is a presentation choice only and does not affect the analysis.
questions_for_user: Layer number: do you have an AFM height, optical-contrast or PL/reflectance result for this flake? The Raman separation alone (60.7 cm⁻¹) is consistent with mono- or few-layer but does not settle it.

Laser power at the sample for each wavelength: was it measured with a power meter at the objective for the dye laser across the sweep? If not, the resonance profile is only trustworthy in relative terms within the 585–611 nm plateau.
Is there a PL spectrum at 4 K on this spot (e.g. off-resonance excitation at 638 nm, or a broadband lamp)? This would confirm whether the ~2.00–2.02 eV background is exciton/trion PL.
Were the spectra dark-subtracted, and was the background subtracted in any way? Several spectra have negative counts, which suggests an offset or subtraction issue.
Is the 140–150 cm⁻¹ step and the 650–700 cm⁻¹ roll-off the notch or edge filter? A blank-substrate measurement or a filter-free measurement would confirm or rule this out.

Was the parallel (co-linear) polarization configuration the same for every excitation? Cross-polarized spectra would help assign the 350 cm⁻¹ and ~480 cm⁻¹ bands and separate E′ from 2LA(M)-type contributions.
Is the 2.14 eV (579 nm) drop real, or a power effect? A repeat at 579 nm with the power measured would settle it.
